“How was school?” asked Dhruv, dropping his bag.
“Fine,” said Yogesh, his face flat as a wall.
“Your face is doing the wall thing. Did somebody say something?”
Yogesh looked at the floor. “They call me Stick. I just look at nothing so they get bored.”
“Does it work?”
“A bit. It also feels like a stone in my stomach.”
“I'm glad you told me. Want me to come and talk to Sir?”
“Maybe. Not yet.”
“Okay. I'll ask again tomorrow.”

qa.q: What do the boys call Yogesh?
qa.a: They call him Stick.

qa.q: What is Yogesh feeling behind his blank face?
qa.a: Hurt, and probably ashamed, since he says it feels like a stone in his stomach. He keeps his face still so the boys get bored and stop.

qa.q: What could Dhruv do next?
qa.a: Respect Yogesh's pace, keep checking in, and be ready to go with him to talk to Sir when he is ready.

qa.q: How might Dhruv see his brother's blank face?
qa.a: He can tell it is not calm, since he calls it “the wall thing”, so he is probably worried and wants to help.

grounding: A child keeps a blank face when teased; an adult checks in privately and offers help.

subtype: Blank face at bullying or shame [Regulating]
passage: I'm Dilnaz. When the girls at the bus stop laughed about my haircut, I made my face like a stone. I didn't blink or smile. Inside I was shaking. At lunch I didn't eat, and Maria Ma'am, my class teacher, noticed. She sat down beside me and said quietly, “The bus stop seemed hard today. You can tell me, or you can help me with the library books. Either is fine.” I chose the books. After a while I said, “They laughed at my hair.” She said, “Thank you for telling me. You can come to me any time.”

qa.q: What did Maria Ma'am ask Dilnaz to help with as an alternative to talking?
qa.a: She offered that Dilnaz could help her with the library books.

qa.q: What was Dilnaz feeling behind her stone face?
qa.a: Hurt and ashamed, since she says inside she was shaking. She kept her face blank so as not to give the girls a reaction.

qa.q: What did Maria Ma'am do that made it easier to talk?
qa.a: She spoke quietly and privately, gave Dilnaz a choice and an easy task, and said she could come any time.

qa.q: How might the girls at the bus stop have read Dilnaz's stone face?
qa.a: They may have thought she did not care, and not seen the hurt behind it.

grounding: A child holds a blank face when teased, which hides real hurt; a private check-in helps.

passage: Note to the school counsellor, Tuesday. Vandana, Class 6. This is the third time I've seen a group near the water cooler comment on Nandini's cracked shoes. Each time her face goes completely still: no frown, no tears, eyes fixed somewhere past them, as if she can't hear. Today I asked her to help me carry books to the staff room. There I said, “I've noticed the comments. You don't have to act like they don't hurt. I can help.” She kept the same blank face for a moment, then said, “They do it every day.” I spoke to the group this afternoon. Please see Nandini before home time. Counsellor's reply, below: Seeing her at 2:30 today.

qa.a: The group has been commenting on Nandini's cracked shoes.

qa.q: What was Nandini most likely feeling behind her still face?
qa.a: She was most likely hurt and ashamed by the daily comments, keeping her face still so the group got no reaction.

qa.q: What steps did Vandana take, and why do they help?
qa.a: Vandana checked in privately, said Nandini didn't have to pretend and offered help, then spoke to the group and asked the counsellor to see Nandini that day.

qa.q: Why might the group think the comments don't matter?

grounding: Shows a child keeping a blank face under teasing to avoid giving a reaction, and a teacher checking in privately and getting help the same day.

subtype: Blank face at bullying or shame [Regulating]
passage: At the village school near the paddy fields in Goa, the boys at the back had a new song about Francis's patched shorts. Francis sat with his face flat as a slate, eyes on the blackboard, hands still on the desk. He didn't blink when a paper ball hit his ear. Hansa Teacher saw it land. She didn't make a scene. At the lunch bell she asked Francis to help her fill the water pot at the well. There she said, “A face can stay very still when something hurts. You can tell me.” His jaw tightened, then let go. He told her. That afternoon she kept the back row behind and sent a note home to Francis's mother.

qa.q: What hit Francis's ear?
qa.a: A paper ball hit his ear.

qa.q: What was Francis likely feeling behind his flat face?
qa.a: He was likely hurt and humiliated by the song, keeping his face still so the boys got no reaction.

qa.q: How did Hansa Teacher make it safe for Francis to speak?
qa.a: She took him to the well away from the others and told him a still face can hide hurt and that he could tell her.

qa.q: What would change if Hansa had scolded the boys in front of everyone at once?
qa.a: Francis might feel even more exposed and might not tell her what had really been happening.

grounding: Shows a child keeping a rigid, blank face while teased, and a teacher checking in privately and acting the same day.

subtype: Blank face at bullying or shame [Regulating]
passage:
At break in the Birmingham schoolyard, three older girls circled Amara. "Nice broom on your head," one said, flicking her braids.

Amara stared straight ahead. Her face didn't move at all: no blink, no frown. The girls got bored and drifted off.

Mr Tomas Novak, on yard duty, had seen it from the steps. Her jaw was locked, and her fists were white at the knuckles. After lunch he asked her to help carry the reading books. In the empty corridor he said, "I saw break. You gave them nothing, but that doesn't mean it didn't hurt."

Amara's chin wobbled. "It happens every day."

"Thank you for telling me. I'm going to the head of year right after this, and you can come to me any time."

qa.q: What did one of the girls say about Amara's braids?
qa.a: "Nice broom on your head."

qa.q: What was Amara likely feeling behind her still face?
qa.a: Hurt and ashamed, holding back every reaction so the girls would get bored; her locked jaw and white knuckles show the strain. It may also have been anger she was keeping down.

qa.q: What did Mr Novak do that made it easier for Amara to speak?
qa.a: He checked in privately with an errand, gently named what he had seen, then acted the same day by going to the head of year and telling her she could come to him any time.

qa.q: What would change if Mr Novak had judged only by Amara's blank face?
qa.a: He might have thought the teasing didn't bother her, and she could have gone on being teased every day without help.

grounding: It shows a child keeping a rigid blank face while teased to give no reaction, and a teacher checking in privately and acting that day.
